notes: CODE DISCREPANCY: task context called WS "Western Sahara", but in this database WS is Samoa (ISO 3166-1); Western Sahara is EH and was assigned to a different repair batch. Verified as Samoa.

Samoa DOES have survey data - World Bank PIP has Samoa HIES 2002/2008/2013 (api.worldbank.org/pip/v1). Latest 2013 national consumption: mean $11.28/day, median $8.38/day, gini 0.387. No MA-anchor derivation needed.

Old values (40/85/180/380/720) understated the bottom half: p50 180 vs PIP median $8.38/day x30.44 = 255/mo (-29%). Corrected set derived from PIP decile shares: p10/p90 from bottom/top decile averages ($3.86/$26.14 per day), p25/p75 from 3rd/8th decile averages, p50 = PIP median directly; daily->monthly x30.44.
First-pass flag ("p50 low vs GDP pc PPP") confirmed and now fixed with primary data.
No household survey exists for Sint Maarten (not in WB PIP; no WID.world entry); old dataSource was the placeholder family label.

Derived from verified NL anchor x PPP GDP-per-capita ratio 0.643 (WB 2023: SXM $51,729 vs NLD $80,392 - Sint Maarten HAS an ICP PPP figure): {"p10": 800, "p25": 1350, "p50": 2060, "p75": 2900, "p90": 3920}
Old p50 1977 was within 4% of derived 2050 - central value essentially confirmed; tails were too compressed (old p10 1414 vs derived ~800), so full set harmonized to anchor shape.
World Bank PIP has South Sudan NBHS 2009 and HIES 2016 (national consumption). Latest 2016: mean $2.34/day, median $1.65/day, gini 0.4405.

Old set (8/18/40/90/210) was flagged unverifiable (dataSource ILO, no credible post-2011 income distribution). Replaced with PIP 2016 decile-derived values: p10/p90 from bottom/top decile averages ($0.57/$5.79 per day), p25/p75 from 3rd/8th decile averages ($0.99/$2.88), p50 = PIP median; daily->monthly x30.44.
Note: PIP 2016 is pre-inflation-crisis; current living standards are likely lower still, but 2016 is the newest primary survey - kept as best available evidence.

World Bank PIP now carries Suriname 2022 national household survey (consumption): mean $18.70/day, median $14.44/day, gini 0.3918. Old entry carried the placeholder-family dataSource with unverifiable values.

Old set (560/653/793/1042/1353) is ~80% above the PIP median at p50 (793 vs 439) and nearly flat p10-p25 (the odd 510/529 segment flagged in pass 1). Replaced with PIP 2022 decile-derived values: p10/p90 from bottom/top decile averages ($5.55/$42.62 per day), p25/p75 from 3rd/8th decile averages ($9.40/$22.73), p50 = PIP median; daily->monthly x30.44.
2022 survey captures the post-2020 currency/inflation crisis - low level vs old values is real, not an error.

No household income/consumption survey exists for Svalbard (not in WB PIP, no WID.world entry). Statistics Norway (SSB) does run wage/tax statistics covering Svalbard, but publishes no public percentile distribution.

SSB report "Svalbard: Population, economy and living conditions" (ssb.no, 2024 data) states Longyearbyen finances/living conditions are "somewhat above average for a Norwegian local community"; Svalbard wages historically carry a small premium over the mainland (harsh-condition allowances; ~50% private-sector employment incl. tourism/logistics).

Old set was NO-derived at ~0.95x mainland - direction contradicted by SSB evidence. Re-derived from verified NO anchor x 1.05: p10 1600, p25 2600, p50 4000, p75 5600, p90 7600. Shape preserved from Norway; level adjusted for the documented premium.

World Bank PIP added Syria HBS 2022 (national consumption) - first Syrian survey since 2009: mean $5.16/day, median $4.61/day, gini 0.2637 (extremely compressed distribution after 12 years of conflict and currency collapse).

Old set (15/32/70/155/340) had a plausible median-ish level but a far too unequal shape (implied gini ~0.45+ vs actual 0.26). Replaced with PIP 2022 decile-derived values: p10/p90 from bottom/top decile averages ($2.39/$9.06 per day), p25/p75 from 3rd/8th decile averages ($3.36/$6.67), p50 = PIP median; daily->monthly x30.44.
Caveat noted: 2022 fieldwork predates the Dec-2024 regime change; no newer survey exists as of Aug 2026.
